body:
Hi, I can see that `_wait_for_events` is being used in other (less latency sensitive?) contexts, such as clipboard handling. I'm personally kinda concerned that changing the timeout might cause other regressions.

Perhaps we could make the timeout configurable and change it only in the polling loop? That sounds like the safest option to me.

> Hi, I can see that `_wait_for_events` is being used in other (less latency sensitive?) contexts, such as clipboard handling. I'm personally kinda concerned that changing the timeout might cause other regressions.
> 
> Perhaps we could make the timeout configurable and change it only in the polling loop? That sounds like the safest option to me.

That sounds like a great idea, good catch! I think I should just edit this PR to change the signature of `_wait_for_events()` to also take a timeout value argument, and give it a default value of 1 second so other call sites don't need to change except the input one. Seems like the least hassle, but I'm not entirely sure about Godot's code-style rules regarding optional arguments as this would be my first contribution (I've read through some of the contributing docs but I may have missed it). Does the community generally prefer only explicit parameters and a refactor of old call sites, or is an optional argument fine?

Happy to do whatever needs done to get this in for 4.6!

Okay, I believe I did the rebase and amend commits properly so there's still only 1 commit for the PR, and I added both `timeout_seconds` and `timeout_microseconds` as `int` parameters to `_wait_for_events()` with the current behaviour as default, and now we should only be lowering the timeout from `_poll_events()`.

I believe using just plain ints is okay here as `timeval.tv_sec` and `timeval.tv_usec` should aways be signed integer types of large enough size that the direct assignment shouldn't be a problem. On my machine's implementation they're `time_t` and `long`, respectively (where `time_t` is just `long int` through a long chain of defines).

I considered adding asserts / comments to make sure we don't ever accidentally pass negative timeout values, or > 1,000,000 values for `timeout_microseconds`, but I tend to over-document, and I think their usage should be pretty clear, so I held off on that.

If more changes are required (or if I goofed up somewhere along the rebase / amend process) please do let me know!
Oops! I noticed that I added an extra newline that caused the code style check to fail. Should be fixed now!
Thanks! And congrats for your first merged Godot contribution :tada:
